description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges. Exploitation of a software vulnerability occurs when an adversary takes advantage of a programming error in a program, service, or within the operating system software or kernel itself to execute adversary-controlled code at a higher privilege level than the current user. Common targets include kernel vulnerabilities (e.g. Dirty Pipe CVE-2022-0847, PwnKit CVE-2021-4034), SUID binaries, and container escape vulnerabilities.

falco.trigger_condition: Processes executing setuid/setgid system calls unexpectedly, changes to file capability bits (setcap), or process privilege transitions detected via Falco's evt.type=setuid and evt.type=setgid filters. Container escape attempts often manifest as unexpected mounts or namespace reassignments.

mitigation: Apply kernel patches promptly. Use seccomp-bpf profiles to restrict dangerous syscalls (setuid, setgid, mount, clone with CLONE_NEWUSER). Drop all Linux capabilities not needed by container processes. Run containers as non-root with a read-only root filesystem.
